title: Harness changes can be exercised live against a worktree-built bro-harness without replacing the fleet binary
wanted_capability: A narrow, documented way to run a real harness session (agent loop, promise/HARNESS_EVENT machinery, daemon-injected MCP catalog) on a bro-harness binary built from the current worktree, while every other dispatch keeps using the installed binary. Today the daemon picks the harness binary once, daemon-wide: prepare_harness_child_launch fills WorkerSpawnSpec.bin_override from bin_with_config, which for harness providers is BRO_HARNESS_BIN or the bro-harness on PATH, with no per-provider config override and no per-dispatch or per-brofile override. Validating a turn-machinery change live therefore means installing the new binary for the whole fleet. Standalone `bro-harness -p` from a worktree build runs without the daemon's catalog injection or dispatch context, and the `isolate` binary covers bindings only, not the agent loop; docs/project-guides/validation.md documents neither route for turn-machinery changes.
missing_primitive: per-dispatch harness binary override (or an equivalent documented worktree smoke path) for turn-machinery validation
fallback_used: Relied on unit tests and noted that the live fleet session kept using the pre-change harness binary, so repeated HARNESS_EVENT messages during validation were expected until reinstall/restart.
evidence: src/orchestration/mod.rs prepare_harness_child_launch (bin_override taken from provider.bin_with_config, daemon-wide)
src/orchestration/providers/exec_args.rs bin_with_env / bin_with_config (harness providers: BRO_HARNESS_BIN else bro-harness; no per-provider override)
crates/bro-protocol/src/worker.rs WorkerSpawnSpec.bin_override (field exists; only the daemon-wide value is ever sent)
docs/project-guides/validation.md (isolate covers bindings only; no turn-machinery live-smoke recipe)
notes: Triage trace: still relevant. Each dispatch now spawns a fresh harness process, so an installed binary swap takes effect without restarts, but the binary remains one daemon-wide choice; there is no way to point a single dispatch at a worktree build.
